spatial_claims.claim: G is placed on ray DE from D with DG = AB
H is placed on ray DF from D with DH = AC
Angle GDH is the same as angle EDF since G lies on ray DE and H lies on ray DF
GH is parallel to EF because DG:DE = DH:DF (sides cut proportionally)
Transversal DE crosses parallel lines GH and EF, so angle DGH = angle DEF by I.29
Transversal DF crosses parallel lines GH and EF, so angle DHG = angle DFE by I.29

configuration_map: Triangle DEF with vertex D at origin. G lies on ray DE from D (at distance AB from D). H lies on ray DF from D (at distance AC from D). Since G and H lie on the same rays from D as E and F respectively, angle GDH is identical to angle EDF. The proportionality DG:DE = DH:DF means GH cuts the sides (or extensions) of triangle DEF proportionally from vertex D, making GH parallel to EF. Whether G falls between D and E (when AB less than DE) or beyond E (when AB greater than DE), the angle equalities from I.29 hold: angle DGH = angle DEF and angle DHG = angle DFE. Verified by coordinate computation in both the internal and external cases.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The construction places G on ray DE and H on ray DF from common vertex D, making angle GDH identical to angle EDF. The proportional cutting yields GH parallel to EF, and I.29 correctly transfers angles regardless of whether G/H fall between D and E/F or beyond them. Coordinate verification confirms angle DGH = angle DEF and angle DHG = angle DFE in both configurations. No angle decomposition issues or interior/exterior contradictions are present.
